translate_en|mods/JeevesDrops/42/media/l: Periodically drop random supply crates near online players. When disabled, airdrops can still be triggered via bot commands and the Airdrop Radio item.
Real seconds between checks for expired or emptied crates. Higher values cost the server less; crates are removed up to this long after they expire. Default 30.

Lets players craft the Airdrop Radio instead of only finding it as loot. Off by default, so nothing changes unless you turn it on. The recipe needs Electrical 5 and is built from a radio receiver and a radio transmitter -- both salvaged by dismantling a ham radio -- plus a charged battery, wire, electronics scrap and a screwdriver you keep. It is a learned recipe rather than one every character starts with, and it is deliberately not auto-learned at any skill level, so the setting stays the only way to get it. Turning this off again also takes the recipe back from characters who had learned it, so a server can withdraw it without a wipe. Radios already in an inventory are never touched either way.

Items listed here never spawn in any drop crate. One shared list respected by every crate type and by Supply Event crates. 
Separate entries with commas. Spacing and capitalization are ignored. 
Each entry can be a full item id (Base.Axe) or just the item name (Axe), which matches that item from any mod. 
Example:  Base.Axe, Pistol, ShotgunShells, WaterBottleFull 
Leave blank to disable.
Include Food/Drink crates in the random auto-drop pool.
Include Literature/Entertainment crates (skill books, skill VHS tapes, and JeevesPC training disks/games if installed) in the random auto-drop pool.
Include Materials crates in the random auto-drop pool.
Include Medical crates in the random auto-drop pool.
Include Military crates in the random auto-drop pool.
Include Tools/Melee crates in the random auto-drop pool.
Hours before an uncollected crate disappears.
Maximum distance from targeted player where crate lands.
Minimum distance from targeted player where crate lands.

When on, players with the Admin access level receive no airdrops at all: they are skipped by automatic and bot random targeting, an Admin who uses an Airdrop Radio gets no drop (and the radio is not consumed), and a bot command that names an Admin is refused. Supply Events are map-wide and unaffected. Only the Admin access level is excluded — Moderator, Overseer, GM, and Observer still receive drops. Off by default.

How long a reserved drop waits to be collected before it is written off, in in-game hours. The clock runs while the server is up whether or not the player is online, and a reservation survives a restart. Nothing is left in the world when one expires, since the crate was never created.

Maximum distance from the targeted player where a crate lands, when Extended Drop Range is on. Distance is picked evenly between min and max, so these two values decide how often a drop is close enough to arrive instantly (90 tiles or less) versus far enough to be a journey. At the default 50-200, roughly a quarter arrive instantly.
Minimum distance from the targeted player where a crate lands, when Extended Drop Range is on. Only used while that setting is enabled.

Lets personal airdrops land much further away than the normal 90-tile limit. A crate can only be created on ground the server currently has loaded, so a drop rolled beyond that limit is reserved instead: you are told where it came down and given a marker, and the crate is placed for real once you get close. Everything after that is an ordinary airdrop, and its despawn timer starts when it appears rather than when it was announced. While this is on, Drop Radius Min/Max are ignored and the Extended values below are used instead. Off by default; turning it off again leaves any drop you are already walking to intact.
How many unique drink items to pick from the pool.
Base amount of each drink. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique food items to pick from the pool.
Base amount of each food item. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique perishable items to pick from the pool. Only used when Include Perishables is enabled.
Base amount of each perishable item. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value. Only used when Include Perishables is enabled.

Add a perishables sub-category to food/drink crates. Drops always arrive fresh — perishables spawn at full freshness regardless of world apocalypse age, then perish naturally over time on their normal shelf-life timeline. Off by default.
Maximum in-game days between automatic air drops. Exact hour within the day-range is randomized.
Minimum in-game days between automatic air drops. Exact hour within the day-range is randomized.

How strongly group size is neutralized (only applies when Group Fairness is on). 100 = a group of any size counts as a single player, equal to a solo. 0 = a group counts as all its members (legacy behavior, larger groups favored). Values in between scale linearly.

When on, auto-drops are distributed between groups instead of individual players, so a large faction or safehouse does not collectively receive far more drops than solo players. Players are grouped by shared vanilla faction or shared safehouse. Off by default.
How many unique skill books to pick. Each spawns exactly 1 copy.
How many JeevesPC skill training disks to pick. Only applies if JeevesPC is installed.
How many video games to pick (vanilla handheld, plus JeevesPC arcade floppies if installed).
How many recipe magazines/schematics to pick (literature that teaches a crafting recipe). Each spawns exactly 1 copy.
How many VHS tapes to pick. Each is stamped with a random skill recording that grants XP when watched.
How many unique fixings & wire items (nails, screws, hinges, wire, rope) to pick.
Base amount of each fixings/wire item. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique lumber & masonry items (planks, logs, bricks) to pick.
Base amount of each lumber/masonry item. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique metal stock items (bars, pipes, sheet, scrap) to pick.
Base amount of each metal stock item. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
Medical: First Aid Kit / Bag Chance (%%)
Percent chance a Medical crate also contains one first aid kit or medical bag. 0 disables it, 100 always includes one.
How many unique medications to pick from the pool.
Base amount of each medication. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique medical supplies to pick from the pool.
Base amount of each supply. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.

Percent chance that an ammo pick which landed on a carton stays a carton instead of becoming that calibre's box. A carton opens to 12 boxes (240 rounds), a box to 20. 0 = boxes only, 100 = cartons as often as boxes.
How many cartons spawn for an ammo type that stays a carton. Exact - cartons take no quantity variance, unlike boxes.
How many unique ammo types to pick. Ammo matching prioritizes rounds for the firearms in this crate.
Base amount of each ammo type. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value.
How many unique firearms to pick. Each spawns exactly 1 copy plus 2 matching magazines (or extra ammo for shotguns).
How many unique gear items (armor, backpacks, clothing) to pick. Each spawns exactly 1 copy.
Players within this range see a directional marker.

How much open space a personal airdrop needs around its landing tile so the crate never clips a wall or building. 0 checks only the landing tile; 1 (default) requires a clear 3x3; higher values demand more open ground and can make crowded areas harder to drop into.
Allow Airdrop Radio items to spawn in the world and be used by players to call in supply drops.
Relative spawn weight (1 = extremely rare, 100 = common). Default 10.

Refuses to drop a crate on map cells that are not connected to any spawn region. Mods that give a vehicle a walk-in interior work by teleporting you onto a separate map of their own, so a drop called from inside one used to land out there, behind walls, on ground you could never reach. Leave this on unless drops stop working on an unusual map layout, where turning it off restores the previous behaviour.
Audible range of the crate alarm at the event site. A single alarm plays for all three crates. Default 100.

How much clear space each supply crate requires around its footprint. 2 (default) requires a clear 5x5. Higher demands more open ground so crates land well away from walls; lower makes tight spots usable.
How far the three supply crates spread out from the event center before each searches for open ground. Larger values scatter the crates over a wider area. Default 15.
Hours before supply event crates disappear. Timer starts when the event is scheduled, not when players arrive. Default 24.
Large-scale supply events at fixed map locations. Three boosted crates (Military, Food, Medical) spawn with heavy zombie resistance. Events are server-wide and broadcast to all players.
Unique drink items in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each drink in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier.
Unique food items in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each food item in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier.
Unique perishable items in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. Only used when Include Perishables is enabled. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each perishable in the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier. Only used when Include Perishables is enabled.
Add a perishables sub-category to the Supply Event Food/Drink crate. Drops arrive fresh (full freshness regardless of world age), then perish naturally. Off by default.
Maximum in-game days between supply events. Default 14 (2 weeks). Exact hour within the day-range is randomized.
Minimum in-game days between supply events. Default 7 (1 week). Exact hour within the day-range is randomized.
Boost multiplier applied to all three event crates. Higher values increase item picks and quantities. Default 2x.
In-game minutes of zombie lure pulses after all zombies have spawned. Keeps zombies moving toward the event site. Default 60.
Radius of zombie attraction pulses at the event center. Larger values draw zombies from further away. Default 300.
Medical: First Aid Kit / Bag Chance (%%)
Percent chance the Supply Event Medical crate also contains one first aid kit or medical bag. 0 disables it, 100 always includes one.
Unique medications in the Supply Event Medical crate. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each medication in the Supply Event Medical crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier.
Unique medical supplies in the Supply Event Medical crate. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each medical supply in the Supply Event Medical crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier.

Percent chance that an ammo pick which landed on a carton stays a carton in the Supply Event Military crate, instead of becoming that calibre's box. A carton opens to 12 boxes (240 rounds), a box to 20. 0 = boxes only, 100 = cartons as often as boxes.
How many cartons spawn for an ammo type that stays a carton in the Supply Event Military crate. Exact - cartons take no quantity variance. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Unique ammo types in the Supply Event Military crate. Matching prioritizes rounds for the firearms in the crate. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Base amount of each ammo type in the Supply Event Military crate. Actual quantity varies from -1 to +3 of this value, then scaled by the Loot Multiplier.
Unique firearms in the Supply Event Military crate. Each spawns 1 copy plus matching magazines (or extra ammo for shotguns). The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.
Unique gear items (armor, backpacks, clothing) in the Supply Event Military crate. Each spawns 1 copy. The Loot Multiplier scales this on top.

How far each supply crate may search outward from its spread position to find genuinely open ground. Higher values almost guarantee all three crates land in the open (never inside a building), at the cost of a larger event footprint. Default 50.
Distance at which the Supply Event moodle appears for players. Default 1000.
In-game minutes over which zombies gradually spawn after players arrive. Default 60.
First in-game day supply events can begin. Default 14.
Total zombies spawned at the event site when players arrive. Max 500. Default 200.
Maximum distance from event center where zombies spawn. Default 80.
Minimum distance from event center where zombies spawn. Default 30.

Relative chance an event zombie wears a civilian outfit (medical, trades, generic, inmate, etc.). Low-value loot. Raise it to make event corpses less rewarding relative to the crates. 0 disables the category. Default 10.
Relative chance an event zombie wears a bandit, raider, biker, thug, or punk outfit. 0 disables the category. Default 15.

Relative chance an event zombie wears a military outfit (Army camo, service uniform, Veteran, Ghillie). These carry the most valuable lootable gear, which can out-value the crates. Lower it to reduce loot piñatas. 0 disables the category. Default 30. Includes the Army instructor outfit.
Supply Event - Zombie Type: Outdoorsman Weight
Relative chance a supply-event zombie wears a ranger, hunter, or private-militia outfit. Was part of the old combined Tactical weight. 0 disables the category. Default 7.

Relative chance an event zombie wears a police, riot, security, prison-guard, or fireman outfit. Also high-value loot. 0 disables the category. Default 25. Includes SWAT, sheriff's deputy and the full fireman suit.
Supply Event - Zombie Type: Survivalist Weight

Relative chance a supply-event zombie wears one of the five Survivalist outfits - the survivor look, carrying packs, tools and boots. Separate from Outdoorsman so survivors can be weighted on their own. 0 disables the category. Default 13.
Danger level shown by the drop's zone moodle: 1 low (shield), 2 medium (warning), 3 high (skull). Default 3.
Creates a temporary Jeeve's Zones danger/PvP zone around each supply drop, removed when the event ends. Requires Jeeve's Zones installed; otherwise has no effect. Default ON.
If ON, the drop's zone is flagged PvP (a hot pocket on an otherwise-safe map when Default-PvP is off). Requires the server PVP setting ON to have any effect. Default ON.
Half-size of the drop's danger/PvP zone, in tiles from the center. 60 covers a 120x120 area. Match it to your zombie spawn radius so the fighting stays inside the marked zone. Default 60.

If ON, the drop's danger/PvP zone is drawn on the player world map. If OFF, the zone still applies (PvP, danger moodle, zombies) but is hidden from the map, so players feel it without seeing the outline. Requires Jeeve's Zones installed. Default ON.
How many unique melee weapons to pick. Each spawns exactly 1 copy.
How many unique tools to pick. Each spawns exactly 1 copy.
Number of zombies that spawn around the crate when it lands. Set to 0 to disable.
Maximum radius around the crate where zombies spawn. Each zombie picks a random radius between min and max.
Minimum radius around the crate where zombies spawn.

Relative chance an airdrop zombie wears a civilian outfit (medical, trades, generic, inmate, etc.). Low-value loot. Raise it to make airdrop corpses less rewarding. 0 disables the category. Default 45.
Relative chance an airdrop zombie wears a bandit, raider, biker, thug, or punk outfit. 0 disables the category. Default 10.
